key_insight: Physical danger in embodied-agent planning is a distinct signal from ordinary text-level safety, and it can be detected from LLM hidden states with a simple linear probe.
engineering_relevance: This enables safer robot and agent planners by filtering grounded physical-risk instructions without over-blocking benign tasks that merely mention risky words.
method: Analyze hidden-state directions to test whether content danger (CD) and physical danger (PD) separate in representation space.
Train PRISM, a single-layer L2-regularized logistic probe on full hidden states.
Validate with random-split null tests and contrastive benchmarks that remove direct harm keywords.
evidence_signal: Across multiple models, PRISM reached 86.2–87.7% accuracy on SafeAgentBench and 99.6% accuracy with 0.7% FPR on PSB-1K, while same-scale LLM judges produced much higher false-positive rates.
watch_item: Results depend on hidden-state access and benchmark design, so real-world deployment should check robustness under distribution shift, new embodiments, and adversarial prompt variation.
paper_title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
